value.behaviour: Home card content listing the signed-in user's latest unread notifications with deep links, mark-as-read, empty, error and loading states, refreshed by signals or by polling.
rules: 1. Destructure props with defaults limit = 5 and pollingIntervalMs = 60000; UnreadNotificationsCardProps carries a TSDoc comment with @public and a TSDoc line on each field (limit: maximum number of notifications shown, default 5; pollingIntervalMs: refresh interval used only when signals are unavailable, default 60000).

2. Hooks, all called unconditionally and in this order: useTranslationRef(notificationsTranslationRef); useApi(notificationsApiRef); useApi(toastApiRef) with toastApiRef from '@backstage/frontend-plugin-api'; the route root per the 'Deep-link href and route fallback' decision; useSignal<NotificationSignal>('notifications') giving lastSignal and isSignalsAvailable; useNotificationsApi from '../../hooks' calling api.getNotifications({ read: false, limit, sort: 'created', sortOrder: 'desc' }) with deps [limit].
3. Local state items: Notification[] | undefined, set to value.notifications by an effect on [value] whenever value is defined.

4. Refresh: const [refresh, setRefresh] = useState(false); throttledSetRefresh = useMemo(() => throttle(setRefresh, 2000), []); an effect calls retry() and setRefresh(false) when refresh is true and loading is false; an effect on [lastSignal, throttledSetRefresh] calls throttledSetRefresh(true) when lastSignal?.action is set; an effect returns () => throttledSetRefresh.cancel().

5. Polling: an effect on [isSignalsAvailable, pollingIntervalMs] returns early when isSignalsAvailable is true; otherwise it starts setInterval(() => setRefresh(true), pollingIntervalMs) and returns a cleanup that calls clearInterval.

6. Mark as read: an onMarkAsRead(id) callback calls notificationsApi.updateNotifications({ ids: [id], read: true }); on success it sets items to the previous items without that id; on rejection it calls toastApi.post({ title: t('unreadNotificationsCard.errors.markAsReadFailed'), status: 'danger' }) and leaves items unchanged.

7. Render in this order: if error, return <ResponseErrorPanel error={error} />; if items is undefined, return <Progress />; otherwise a Flex direction column gap 3 holding either <Text variant="body-medium" color="secondary"> with t('unreadNotificationsCard.emptyMessage') when items is empty, or one row per item, followed by a <Link to={root}> with t('unreadNotificationsCard.viewAll').

8. Each row is a Flex gap 3 align center with key notification.id: <NotificationIcon notification={notification} /> imported from '../NotificationsTable/NotificationIcon'; a Flex direction column gap 1 holding <Text variant="body-medium"> wrapping <Link to={`${root}?id=${encodeURIComponent(notification.id)}`}>{notification.payload.title}</Link> and <Text variant="body-small" color="secondary"> wrapping <RelativeTime value={notification.created} /> (imported as in NotificationsTable.tsx with the // @ts-ignore line); then <ButtonIcon aria-label={t('unreadNotificationsCard.markAsRead')} icon={<RiCheckboxCircleLine size={16} />} variant="secondary" onPress={() => onMarkAsRead(notification.id)} />.

9. Link, Progress and ResponseErrorPanel come from '@backstage/core-components'; Flex, Text and ButtonIcon from '@backstage/ui'; useApi and useRouteRef from '@backstage/core-plugin-api'; rootRouteRef from '../../routes'; notificationsApiRef from '../../api'.
10. UnreadNotificationsCardContent is a named function export with no release tag in its TSDoc (it is not part of the package entry).

value.behaviour: jsdom tests of the card: list, deep links, empty and error states, mark-as-read, signal refetch, polling and unmount cleanup.
rules: 1. Render <UnreadNotificationsCardContent /> (or with props) inside TestApiProvider through renderInTestApp; the notifications API mock provides getNotifications and updateNotifications as jest.fn(); a toast mock provides post: jest.fn().

2. The signals case provides signalApiRef with { subscribe: jest.fn((_channel, onMessage) => { publish = onMessage; return { unsubscribe: jest.fn() }; }) } and calls publish({ action: 'new_notification', notification_id: 'n3' }) inside act; cases without signals omit signalApiRef so isSignalsAvailable is false.
3. Timer cases call jest.useFakeTimers() before rendering, advance with act(() => { jest.advanceTimersByTime(ms); }), and restore real timers in afterEach; reset mocks in beforeEach.
4. The deep-link case passes mountedRoutes: { '/notifications': rootRouteRef } to renderInTestApp, with rootRouteRef from '../../routes'.
5. Click buttons with fireEvent.click on screen.getAllByRole('button', { name: 'Mark as read' }); wait for removal with waitForElementToBeRemoved.

style_from.reason: Test file header, renderInTestApp and screen usage in this package.

uses.reason: notificationsApiRef and the NotificationsApi type for the mock.

tests.name: lists unread notifications newest first with deep links
tests.given: getNotifications resolves { notifications: [n1 'Newest' created 2026-10-29, n2 'Older' created 2026-10-28 with id 'n/2'], totalCount: 2 }, rendered with the notifications route mounted
tests.expect: 'Newest' appears before 'Older' in document order; getNotifications was called once with { read: false, limit: 5, sort: 'created', sortOrder: 'desc' }; the 'Newest' link href is '/notifications?id=n1' and the 'Older' link href is '/notifications?id=n%2F2'; a 'View all notifications' link points to '/notifications'

tests.name: honours the limit prop
tests.given: rendered with limit={3} and getNotifications resolving an empty list
tests.expect: getNotifications was called with limit: 3 and 'No unread notifications' is shown

tests.name: shows the error state when fetching fails
tests.expect: screen.findAllByText('Boom') finds at least one element (the error panel may repeat the message), no notification list item or 'Mark as read' button is present, and the card does not throw

tests.name: marks a notification as read and removes it, and keeps it when the update fails
tests.given: two unread notifications; updateNotifications resolves for the first click and rejects for the second
tests.expect: after clicking 'Mark as read' on 'Newest', updateNotifications was called with { ids: ['n1'], read: true } and 'Newest' is removed; after clicking it on 'Older', updateNotifications was called with { ids: ['n/2'], read: true }, 'Older' is still shown and the toast mock's post was called with { title: 'Failed to mark notification as read', status: 'danger' }

tests.name: refetches when a notifications signal arrives
tests.given: the signal API mock is provided and the first list has rendered
tests.expect: getNotifications has one call; after publishing a new_notification signal it has two calls and the list shows the second response's title

tests.name: polls when signals are unavailable and stops after unmount
tests.given: no signal API, fake timers, the first list rendered
tests.expect: advancing 59999 ms keeps one getNotifications call; advancing 1 ms more makes two calls; after unmount, advancing 180000 ms keeps two calls

tests.name: does not poll when signals are available
tests.given: the signal API mock is provided, fake timers, the first list rendered
tests.expect: advancing 180000 ms keeps one getNotifications call
